## In the MRP

The outlook projects the likely direction of the rating and never changes the current rating class. Its base input is the projected change in the country's distance to losing the good equilibrium over the next year along the announced fiscal path. Information beyond the model may adjust it with published justification: backstop politics, banking stress, investor-base shifts, a material captive creditor layer.

## In the DAP

Every issue a team deems relevant enters the outlook. The country team synthesizes related issues into one story (e.g., a competitiveness gap, its labour-cost measurement, and fiscal-politics flags) rather than listing them. Developments that fit no parameter (elections, banking events, geopolitical shocks) enter here, as do market-desk findings. The MRP's conservative design choices (permanent risk-off, no captive creditors, zero recovery, no credit for a positive inflation differential) are noted here when a team considers them materially binding, but are never relaxed.

## Methods by Document Type

### [Country-Specific Recommendations](../document-types/country-specific-recommendations.qmd)

- These documents assess progress on implementing previous recommendations and identify key challenges relevant to the outlook, such as structural challenges, labor shortages, regulatory burdens, and energy inefficiencies. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>
- The documents report on institutional and geopolitical risks, including judicial efficiency, anti-corruption frameworks, energy dependence, and defense spending, which are synthesized as outlook material. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 9" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Slovakia_2026-06-03, p. 9">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 9" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 9">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 9" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 9">ⓘ</button>
- The documents identify macroeconomic imbalances and structural vulnerabilities, such as housing shortages and long-term care spending projections, that inform the qualitative outlook. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/recommendations/Netherlands_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button>

### [Economic Survey](../document-types/economic-survey.qmd)

- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) discusses structural reforms, climate transition costs, and artificial intelligence (AI) adoption as factors affecting long-term growth and fiscal sustainability. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 36" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 36">ⓘ</button>
- The surveys identify specific outlook factors such as political stability, rule of law, euro adoption risks, climate risks, and demographic trends. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 25">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 135" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 135">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 37" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 37">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 94" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 94">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 31">ⓘ</button>
- The reports discuss political stability, banking sector resilience, and demographic pressures as key drivers of future economic performance and sovereign risk. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 8" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 8">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 116" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Austria_2026-03-19, p. 116">ⓘ</button>
- Economic surveys provide structural and qualitative assessments that feed into the outlook, including evaluations of fiscal sustainability, labor market participation, and climate risks. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Belgium_2024-09-23, p. 30">ⓘ</button>
- The document notes heightened political uncertainty and frequent government changes since 2024 have weakened business and household confidence, delaying consumption and investment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 18" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 18">ⓘ</button>
- The document highlights manufacturing deindustrialization, structural shifts, and weaker export performance as drivers of industrial competitiveness concerns. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 13" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 13">ⓘ</button>
- The survey identifies severe demographic headwinds with a rapidly shrinking and aging population, requiring reforms in pensions, healthcare, and labor markets to sustain growth. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Croatia_2026-01-30, p. 11">ⓘ</button>
- The document notes significant security risks from Russia, including cyber-attacks and infrastructure sabotage, contributing to economic uncertainty and defense spending increases. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 25">ⓘ</button>
- The survey identifies geopolitical shocks, such as the war in Ukraine and rising trade tensions, hitting the German economy through supply chain bottlenecks and higher energy prices. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 9">ⓘ</button>
- The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) notes that the balance of risks to the economic outlook is tilted to the downside, citing potential geopolitical tensions, slower growth among main trading partners, and delays in the implementation of the Recovery and Resilience Plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 27" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 27">ⓘ</button>
- The document highlights that Greece is particularly vulnerable to a warming climate, with high risks from forest fires and floods. Extreme weather events, such as the 2023 floods in Thessaly, have caused large economic damages and may become more frequent and severe. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 14" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 14">ⓘ</button>
- Downside risks include escalation of geopolitical tensions, particularly the war in Ukraine and conflicts in the Middle East, which could affect risk premiums and energy prices. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 9">ⓘ</button>
- Labor shortages are exacerbated by a declining working-age population and emigration, contributing to inflationary pressures and rising unit labor costs. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 18" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 18">ⓘ</button>
- The 2026 Middle East conflict has renewed volatility in global energy markets. [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd) remains exposed due to high reliance on imported fossil fuels (74% of net total energy consumed). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 90" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 90">ⓘ</button>
- Global trade policy restrictions and competition from emerging economies (e.g., China) weigh on Italian exports and industrial production. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 22" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 22">ⓘ</button>
- Housing affordability and availability continue to fall short, affecting well-being and competitiveness. Recent policies have increased completions, but structural impediments remain. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 77" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 77">ⓘ</button>
- Ireland is not on track to meet its 2030 greenhouse gas emission targets, having reduced emissions by only 7.8% from 2018 levels against a target of 51%. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 61" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 61">ⓘ</button>
- Labor shortages risk jeopardizing housing and climate reform agendas, with an estimated need for 50,000 additional construction workers by 2030. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 44" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 44">ⓘ</button>
- Lithuania faces a major demographic shock, with the working-age population projected to decline by 30% by 2050. The old-age dependency ratio is expected to exceed 50% by 2050. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 16" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 16">ⓘ</button>
- Recent reversal in net migration, driven by Ukrainian refugees and return migration, could mitigate labour shortages. Simulations suggest extending the recent net migration trend would reduce the projected fall in production by half. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 97" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 97">ⓘ</button>
- The pension system's sustainability is a major long-term risk, with expenditure projected to rise from 9.4% of GDP in 2024 to 17.5% in 2070 without reform. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 54" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 54">ⓘ</button>
- The transition to green growth will have a net negative impact on the budget balance, estimated at around 2% of GDP by 2050, primarily due to lower fuel revenues. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 28, 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 28, 30">ⓘ</button>
- Housing affordability remains low, with real house prices falling by about 20% since late 2022, but affordability deteriorating further due to higher interest rates. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 40" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Luxembourg_2025-04-28, p. 40">ⓘ</button>
- The economic outlook is surrounded by significant downside risks, primarily driven by rising geopolitical tensions and trade fragmentation. The [Netherlands](../countries/netherlands.qmd), as a trade-dependent economy, is exposed to higher tariffs and supply chain disruptions. US tariffs are expected to reduce Dutch GDP growth by one percentage point cumulatively over 2025-26. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 11">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 25">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 29" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- Residential house prices have rebounded strongly since late 2023. The debt-to-income ratio remains high at 203%. The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) advises monitoring the housing market and considering further macroprudential measures, such as lowering the maximum loan-to-value ratio. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 11">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 30" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 30">ⓘ</button>
- The [Netherlands](../countries/netherlands.qmd) is unlikely to reach its 2030 climate targets under current policies due to delays in implementation and policy uncertainty. Grid congestion hinders electrification. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 13" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 13">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 58" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Netherlands_2025-07-09, p. 58">ⓘ</button>
- Trade tensions and geopolitical fragmentation pose significant downside risks. A 25 percentage point increase in US tariffs on the European Union, combined with retaliation, could reduce [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd)'s GDP by 0.7% to 1.1% after three years. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 29" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 29">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD assumes a 15% US tariff on most European exports, including cars and pharmaceuticals, in its baseline projection. This is expected to weigh on [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd)'s exports and private investment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 13" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 13">ⓘ</button>
- [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd) has committed to increasing defense spending to 5% of GDP by 2035, up from 1.5% in 2023, posing additional fiscal pressure. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 35" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 35">ⓘ</button>
- Structural challenges in the housing market, including regulatory barriers to investment and weak rental markets, have undermined affordability. Young people are disproportionately affected. Reforms are needed to remove investment obstacles, use existing housing more effectively, and improve rental markets. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 103" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 103">ⓘ</button>
- [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd) is highly exposed to climate risks, including wildfires, heatwaves, and coastal erosion. Lack of stable funding and weak coordination at the local level hold back adaptation progress. Strengthening private insurance coverage is recommended to reduce contingent liabilities. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 88" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 88">ⓘ</button>
- Mobilising untapped labour market potential requires improving school-to-work transitions, creating enabling environments for older workers, maximising the contribution of foreign workers, and strengthening women’s participation. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 74" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Portugal_2026-01-06, p. 74">ⓘ</button>
- The survey highlights remaining challenges in the anti-corruption framework, including lobbying oversight, whistleblower protection, and the independence of investigators and prosecutors. No foreign bribery cases have been reported or investigated. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 41" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 41">ⓘ</button>
- The economy is exposed to external shocks from the conflict in the Middle East and rising trade protectionism. [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd)'s highly open economy relies heavily on foreign demand and inputs, particularly in the automotive and chemical sectors. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 50" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 50">ⓘ</button>
- The OECD identifies issues with the rule of law and judicial independence. Perceptions of corruption are high, with 85% of companies perceiving corruption as widespread. Recent reforms, including the dissolution of the Special Prosecutor’s Office, have raised concerns about the effectiveness of anti-corruption efforts. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 64-67" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 64-67">ⓘ</button>
- AI adoption in Slovakia is lagging behind EU peers. Only 18% of enterprises reported using AI in 2025, up from 7% in 2023. The OECD recommends streamlining regulation to ease access to data and helping firms comply with the EU AI Act to accelerate adoption. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 11-12, 108-109" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 11-12, 108-109">ⓘ</button>
- Slovakia is well-positioned for the net-zero transition due to its low-carbon electricity mix (nuclear and hydro). However, administrative procedures for low-carbon power projects are cumbersome. The OECD recommends streamlining permitting and moving to market-based electricity pricing while supporting low-income households with targeted transfers. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 13, 129-137" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 13, 129-137">ⓘ</button>
- Severe skills shortages, particularly in the automotive and industrial sectors, hinder growth. The OECD recommends improving the education system, facilitating lifelong learning, and increasing the use of active labor market policies focused on retraining and upskilling. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 89-91" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovakia_2026-06-25, p. 89-91">ⓘ</button>
- SMEs face barriers including limited access to finance, high administrative burdens, and low adoption of advanced digital technologies. Only 26% of SMEs adopted cloud services in 2023, below the EU average. Productivity gaps persist between micro/small firms and large firms. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 13, p. 71" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 13, p. 71">ⓘ</button>
- Population aging is advancing faster than in most OECD countries. The old-age dependency ratio is projected to increase by 41 percentage points by 2054. Employment rates for older workers remain low, and non-contributory unemployment assistance for those over 52 discourages job search. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 14, p. 84, p. 85" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 14, p. 84, p. 85">ⓘ</button>
- Spain is highly exposed to climate risks, with economic losses from disasters among the highest in Europe. Floods, droughts, and heatwaves threaten growth and public finances. Water pricing does not reflect scarcity, undermining efficient use. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 16, p. 101, p. 106" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Spain_2025-11-26, p. 16, p. 101, p. 106">ⓘ</button>

### [Country Report](../document-types/country-report.qmd)

- The [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd)'s country reports provide structural and qualitative assessments that feed into the outlook. These include assessments of structural challenges, energy security, institutional quality, and geopolitical risks. The reports do not directly calculate the MRP outlook but provide the "outlook material" and qualitative flags used in the discretionary adjustments process. <button type="button" class="source-ref" - The document extensively discusses structural reforms, political fragmentation, and regional disparities as key drivers of future economic performance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 7" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Spain_2026-06-03, p. 7">ⓘ</button>

### [Post-Programme Surveillance Report](../document-types/post-programme-surveillance-report.qmd)

- This report presents the results of post-programme surveillance missions conducted by the [European Commission](../institutions/european-commission.qmd), in liaison with the [European Central Bank](../institutions/european-central-bank.qmd), [European Stability Mechanism](../institutions/european-stability-mechanism.qmd), and [International Monetary Fund](../institutions/international-monetary-fund.qmd), for Ireland, Greece, Cyprus, and Portugal in March and April 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2">ⓘ</button>
- The assessments evaluate the economic, fiscal, and financial situations of these euro-area Member States to ensure their capacity to service debt, using macroeconomic and budgetary projections from the Commission’s Spring 2026 Economic Forecast. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2" aria-label="Source: ec/post-programme/Post-Programme-Surveillance-Spring-2026_2026-06-03, p. 2">ⓘ</button>

### [Debt Sustainability Monitor](../document-types/debt-sustainability-monitor.qmd)

- The document employs stochastic projections with 10,000 shocks to assess uncertainty, covering 80% of simulated debt paths. Deterministic stress tests include scenarios for adverse interest-growth differentials, lower structural primary balance, historical structural primary balance, and financial stress. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 122" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 122">ⓘ</button>
- For [Belgium](../countries/belgium.qmd), climate risk under a "Fragmented Action" scenario could increase debt by 3 percentage points of GDP by 2050. Political risk involves lack of effective budgetary coordination. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 123" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 123">ⓘ</button>
- For [Bulgaria](../countries/bulgaria.qmd), non-performing loans in the banking sector are a risk-increasing factor. Climate risk deviations are generally small. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 128" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 128">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 129" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 129">ⓘ</button>
- For [Germany](../countries/germany.qmd), contingent liabilities from debt brake reform and special funds are risk-increasing. Climate risk could increase debt by 3 percentage points of GDP by 2050. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 143" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 143">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109">ⓘ</button>
- For [Estonia](../countries/estonia.qmd), a large share of government debt held by non-residents is a risk-increasing factor. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 148" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 148">ⓘ</button>
- For [Ireland](../countries/ireland.qmd), concentration of tax revenues in multinational enterprises is a risk-increasing factor. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 153" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 153">ⓘ</button>
- For [Greece](../countries/greece.qmd), state guarantees, non-performing loans, negative net international investment position, and pending legal cases are risk-increasing. A major share of debt held by official lenders at low rates is risk-mitigating. Climate risk could increase debt by 6 percentage points of GDP by 2050. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 158" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 158">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109">ⓘ</button>
- For [Spain](../countries/spain.qmd), an increasing share of debt held by non-residents is a risk-increasing factor. Climate risk could increase debt by 6 percentage points of GDP by 2050. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 163" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 163">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109">ⓘ</button>
- For [France](../countries/france.qmd), contingent liability risks from the private sector and state guarantees are risk-increasing. Climate risk could increase debt by 6 percentage points of GDP by 2050. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 168" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 168">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 109">ⓘ</button>
- For [Slovakia](../countries/slovakia.qmd), political stability issues, including broad institutional challenges and political tensions, are noted as outlook material. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 242" aria-label="Source: ec/debt-sustainability/Debt-Sustainability-Monitor-2025_2026-02-12, p. 242">ⓘ</button>

### [Economic Forecast](../document-types/economic-forecast.qmd)

- The forecast incorporates an energy price shock from the Middle East conflict as a key downside risk for the euro area and specific member states, affecting real incomes and investment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 18" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 18">ⓘ</button>
- For [Germany](../countries/germany.qmd), the energy price shock weighs on real incomes, while public spending ramp-up supports growth. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 112" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 112">ⓘ</button>
- For [France](../countries/france.qmd), net exports offset weak private consumption due to higher energy prices. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 122" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 122">ⓘ</button>
- For [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd), domestic demand is dampened by loss of purchasing power and geopolitical tensions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 126" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 126">ⓘ</button>
- For [Spain](../countries/spain.qmd), growth is driven by domestic demand supported by a robust labor market. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 120" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 120">ⓘ</button>
- For [Belgium](../countries/belgium.qmd), private consumption weakens due to reduced purchasing power. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 108" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 108">ⓘ</button>
- For [Greece](../countries/greece.qmd), investment remains robust due to Recovery and Resilience Facility absorption. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 118" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 118">ⓘ</button>
- For [Austria](../countries/austria.qmd), the energy price shock disrupts recovery momentum. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 140" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 140">ⓘ</button>
- For [Netherlands](../countries/netherlands.qmd), structural bottlenecks and global uncertainty dampen consumption and investment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 138" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 138">ⓘ</button>
- For [Portugal](../countries/portugal.qmd), adverse shocks include severe storms and energy price surges. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 142" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 142">ⓘ</button>
- For [Ireland](../countries/ireland.qmd), GDP decline in 2026 is due to base effects from pharmaceutical export frontloading, while domestic activity remains resilient. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 116" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 116">ⓘ</button>
- For [Croatia](../countries/croatia.qmd), domestic demand supports growth, but net exports weigh negatively. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 124" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 124">ⓘ</button>
- For [Cyprus](../countries/cyprus.qmd), tourism exports may be negatively affected by the conflict. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 128" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 128">ⓘ</button>
- For [Estonia](../countries/estonia.qmd), geopolitical concerns weigh on investment and exports. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 114" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 114">ⓘ</button>
- For [Latvia](../countries/latvia.qmd), growth slows due to the Middle East conflict. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 130" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 130">ⓘ</button>
- For [Lithuania](../countries/lithuania.qmd), private consumption is the main driver. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 132" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 132">ⓘ</button>
- For [Luxembourg](../countries/luxembourg.qmd), growth is supported by services exports. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 134" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 134">ⓘ</button>
- For [Malta](../countries/malta.qmd), growth is driven by domestic consumption and services. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 136" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 136">ⓘ</button>
- For [Slovakia](../countries/slovakia.qmd), domestic demand is subdued due to fiscal consolidation. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 146" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 146">ⓘ</button>
- For [Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd), domestic demand drives growth. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 144" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 144">ⓘ</button>
- For [Bulgaria](../countries/bulgaria.qmd), domestic demand growth slows. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 110" aria-label="Source: ec/forecast/Spring-2026-Economic-Forecast_2026-05-21, p. 110">ⓘ</button>

| Country | Latest figures | Red flags with reported evidence | Source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Croatia](../countries/croatia.qmd) | Defence spending 2026e: 1.6% of GDP | Geopolitical shocks: Conflict in the Middle East weighs on outlook; reintroduction of fuel price caps in March 2026. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Croatia_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button> |
| [Bulgaria](../countries/bulgaria.qmd) | Euro adoption January 2026 | Political stability: A period of political instability with seven early elections in four years ended with a government forming in January 2025, which resigned in December 2025. This instability has delayed reforms and disbursement of EU funds. Rule of law: Corruption remains a critical issue. The OECD estimates that reducing corruption to Visegrad-4 levels would raise per capita GDP by 2.1% in the long run. Public procurement is identified as a high-risk area for state capture. Euro adoption risks: A short-term spike in inflation may follow the euro's introduction due to price resetting. The authorities have committed to active surveillance to avoid inflation “rounding-up” effects. Climate risks: Bulgaria is vulnerable to extreme weather events such as floods and droughts. Insurance coverage against catastrophic risks remains extremely limited, with only 2% of all insurance contracts covering climate-related risks. Demographics: The working-age population is shrinking rapidly. Net migration has turned positive since 2020, but emigration of skilled labour remains a serious issue. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 25">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 135" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 135">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 37" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 37">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 94" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 94">ⓘ</button> <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 31" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 31">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Bulgaria_2026-02-05, p. 25">ⓘ</button> |
| [Estonia](../countries/estonia.qmd) | Real GDP growth 2027: 2.7% | Climate transition: Estonia remains among the most carbon-intensive OECD economies. Emissions reductions in transport and agriculture have lagged, and land use/forestry has shifted from a carbon sink to a source. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 11">ⓘ</button> Climate adaptation: Climate risks, particularly flooding, are moderate but require early investment and stronger governance. Municipalities lack financial and administrative capacity for adaptation. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 12" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 12">ⓘ</button> AI adoption: AI adoption is high in knowledge-intensive sectors but lags in traditional sectors. Skill shortages are a key barrier to wider adoption. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 13" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 13">ⓘ</button> Demographics: Adverse demographic trends, with a declining working-age population, will weigh on growth. Immigration has temporarily mitigated this. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 18" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 18">ⓘ</button> Political context: Increased defence spending remains the key policy priority, with a target of above 5% of GDP from 2026 onwards. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 18" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 18">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 11" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Estonia_2026-06-08, p. 11">ⓘ</button> |
| [Cyprus](../countries/cyprus.qmd) | General government debt 2025: 55.0% of GDP | Geopolitical shocks: Conflict in the Middle East poses risks to tourism and investor confidence. Energy security: High dependence on imported oil and delays in interconnection projects. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Cyprus_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button> |
| [Austria](../countries/austria.qmd) | Unit Labour Cost growth 2022–2025: +21% | Geopolitical shocks: Middle East conflict and energy shock threaten recovery. Institutional challenges: Underdeveloped venture and growth capital markets. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Austria_2026-06-03, p. 3">ⓘ</button> |
| [Belgium](../countries/belgium.qmd) | R&D intensity 2024: 3.36% of GDP | Institutional weakness: Budgetary process suffers from structural weaknesses, including lack of multiannual fiscal planning. Energy transition: High dependence on fossil fuel imports. Banking sector: Stable capital-adequacy ratio of 20.2% in Q3-2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 4" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 4">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 10" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Belgium_2026-06-03, p. 10">ⓘ</button> |
| [Finland](../countries/finland.qmd) | Real GDP growth 2026: 1.1% | Geopolitical shocks: Finland faces significant security risks from Russia, including cyber-attacks and infrastructure sabotage. The country closed its border with Russia indefinitely in April 2024 and joined the North Atlantic Treaty Organization in April 2023. These factors contribute to economic uncertainty and defense spending increases. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 25">ⓘ</button> Demographic trends: The working-age population is projected to shrink in the 2030s under baseline migration assumptions, although recent high migration levels have led to upward revisions in population projections. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 39">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 25" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Finland_2025-05-23, p. 25">ⓘ</button> |
| [France](../countries/france.qmd) | Real GDP growth 2026: 0.8% | Political stability: Heightened political uncertainty and frequent government changes since 2024 have weakened business and household confidence, delaying consumption and investment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 18" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 18">ⓘ</button> Geopolitical risks: The evolving conflict in the Middle East has triggered an energy shock that disrupted economic momentum and weighed on investor sentiment. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 9">ⓘ</button> Industrial competitiveness: Manufacturing deindustrialization has been sharper than the OECD average, driven by structural shifts and weaker export performance. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 13" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 13">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 18" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/France_2026-06-30, p. 18">ⓘ</button> |
| [Germany](../countries/germany.qmd) | Real GDP growth 2026f: 1.2% | Geopolitical shocks: Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and rising trade tensions have hit the German economy. Supply chain bottlenecks and higher energy prices have affected the globally integrated German economy more than others. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 9">ⓘ</button> Elections: The fall of the coalition government in November 2024 and the formation of a new government in early 2025 reduced domestic policy uncertainty. A provisional budget was approved for 2025. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 21-22" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 21-22">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Germany_2025-06-12, p. 9">ⓘ</button> |
| [Greece](../countries/greece.qmd) | Public debt 2023: 163.9% of GDP | Geopolitical tensions: Balance of risks tilted to the downside due to potential geopolitical tensions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 27" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 27">ⓘ</button> Climate risks: Vulnerable to warming climate, with high risks from forest fires and floods; 2023 Thessaly floods caused large economic damages. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 14" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 14">ⓘ</button> Policy implementation: Downside risks include slower growth among main trading partners and delays in implementing the Recovery and Resilience Plan. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 27" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 27">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 27" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Greece_2024-12-05, p. 27">ⓘ</button> |
| [Italy](../countries/italy.qmd) | Public debt 2025 (p): 137.1% of GDP | Energy security: Exposure to high reliance on imported fossil fuels (74% of net total energy consumed) amid renewed volatility from the 2026 Middle East conflict. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 90" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 90">ⓘ</button> Trade policy: Global trade policy restrictions and competition from emerging economies (e.g., China) weigh on exports and industrial production. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 22" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 22">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 90" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Italy_2026-04-23, p. 90">ⓘ</button> |
| [Latvia](../countries/latvia.qmd) | General government debt 2027f: 50.3% of GDP | Geopolitical risks: Downside risks from escalation of tensions, particularly the war in Ukraine and Middle East conflicts, affecting risk premiums and energy prices. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 9">ⓘ</button> Labor market: Labor shortages exacerbated by a declining working-age population and emigration, contributing to inflationary pressures. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 18" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 18">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 9" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Latvia_2026-06-12, p. 9">ⓘ</button> |
| [Ireland](../countries/ireland.qmd) | General government balance 2025: 1.7% of GDP | Housing supply: Affordability and availability fall short, affecting competitiveness; structural impediments remain despite increased completions. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 77" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 77">ⓘ</button> Climate policy: Not on track to meet 2030 greenhouse gas emission targets (reduced only 7.8% vs. 51% target). <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 61" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 61">ⓘ</button> Labor shortages: Risk to housing and climate reform agendas; need for 50,000 additional construction workers by 2030. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 44" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 44">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 77" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Ireland_2025-02-12, p. 77">ⓘ</button> |
| [Lithuania](../countries/lithuania.qmd) | General government debt 2026: 43.4% of GDP | Demographics: Major demographic shock with working-age population projected to decline by 30% by 2050; old-age dependency ratio to exceed 50%. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 16" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 16">ⓘ</button> Migration: Recent reversal in net migration (Ukrainian refugees, return migration) could mitigate labor shortages. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 97" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 97">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 16" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Lithuania_2025-03-28, p. 16">ⓘ</button> |
| [Luxembourg](../countries/luxembourg.qmd) | General government balance 2025: -2.0% of GDP | Housing and labor market: House prices 60% higher than a decade ago; unemployment rose to 6.5% in 2025, above EU average. Skills mismatches: Macroeconomic skills mismatches rose to 34.4% in 2025. Pension sustainability: Pillar I reserve projected to deplete by 2048. Tax planning: Net inward FDI stock 31 times larger than GDP. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 22" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Luxembourg_2026-06-03, p. 22">ⓘ</button> |

Transparency: Ministers stopped publicly declaring family income after 2023; no comprehensive rules on lobbying. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 11-12" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 11-12">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 13-14" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Malta_2026-06-03, p. 13-14">ⓘ</button> |

Energy transition: Permits for renewable energy projects are delayed due to complex regulatory frameworks. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 7-8" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 7-8">ⓘ</button> | <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5" aria-label="Source: ec/country-reports/Portugal_2026-06-03, p. 5">ⓘ</button> |

[Slovenia](../countries/slovenia.qmd)'s highly open economy relies heavily on foreign demand and inputs, particularly in the automotive and chemical sectors. <button type="button" class="source-ref" data-source="oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 50" aria-label="Source: oecd/economic-surveys/Slovenia_2026-06-16, p. 50">ⓘ</button> Political stability and rule of law: The [OECD](../institutions/oecd.qmd) highlights remaining challenges in the anti-corruption framework, including lobbying oversight, whistleblower protection, and the independence of investigators and prosecutors. Perceptions of corruption are high, with 85% of companies perceiving corruption as widespread. Structural issues: High child poverty (33.8% at risk of poverty or social exclusion in 2025), skills mismatches, regulatory fragmentation across regions, and a business landscape dominated by micro-enterprises.
